Code and attributes survive, but attributes attach differently and Pandoc line numbering is not implemented.
examples.originalSource:
~~~~ {#mycode .haskell .numberLines startFrom="100"}
qsort []     = []
qsort (x:xs) = qsort (filter (< x) xs) ++ [x] ++
               qsort (filter (>= x) xs)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
examples.source:
~~~~ {#mycode .haskell .numberLines startFrom="100"}
qsort []     = []
qsort (x:xs) = qsort (filter (< x) xs) ++ [x] ++
               qsort (filter (>= x) xs)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

workaround.explanation: Use tp-code-editor in read-only mode with line-numbers. Haskell syntax highlighting loads on demand. Set line-number-start=100 to display 100, 101 and 102, matching Pandoc’s startFrom; id=mycode preserves the target ID. This provides a web editor presentation rather than a static pre/code block.
workaround.source:
:::: tp-code-editor {readonly line-numbers line-number-start=100 id=mycode}
::: script {type="tp/haskell"}
qsort []     = []
qsort (x:xs) = qsort (filter (< x) xs) ++ [x] ++
               qsort (filter (>= x) xs)
:::
::::

pandocMode.explanation: A readonly code editor shows Haskell with line numbers starting at 100.

examples.explanation: TP supports alphabetic and Roman-numeral lists, but this example’s Roman sublist remains part of the parent paragraph because it has no separating blank line and uses varying indentation.

10)  Tenth
11)  Eleventh
       i. subone
      ii. subtwo
     iii. subthree

workaround.explanation: Keep native Markdown lists, including the 9), 10) and 11) markers. Insert a blank line before the Roman sublist and align its markers with a consistent four-space indentation under the decimal list item. TP recognizes a./b., A./B., i./ii. and I./II. lists; no element directives are needed here. The closing parenthesis is accepted as source syntax; the browser normally displays decimal markers with a period.
workaround.source:
9) Ninth
10) Tenth
11) Eleventh

    i. subone
    ii. subtwo
    iii. subthree

```markdown
Term
: Definition
```

examples.explanation: Labeled example lists and their references are not resolved.
examples.originalSource:
(@good)  This is a good example.

As (@good) illustrates, ...
examples.source:
(@good)  This is a good example.

As (@good) illustrates, ...

workaround.explanation: Assign an ID directly to the paragraph, then use an ordinary fragment link. Put {#good} on the next line without a blank line before it, so the ID belongs to the example paragraph. A blank line before the attribute block would instead create a separate empty paragraph with that ID. Maintain the visible example number yourself; Pandoc’s (@good) lookup is not available.

examples.explanation: Repeated example-list labels are not resolved.

Intervening text...

This theory can explain the case we saw earlier (repeated):

(@foo) Sample sentence.

Intervening text...

This theory can explain the case we saw earlier (repeated):

(@foo) Sample sentence.

workaround.explanation: Write the repeated number explicitly and give the original occurrence a unique ID. Do not reuse an HTML ID for the repeated example; link back to the first occurrence instead.
workaround.source:
(1) Sample sentence.
{#foo}

Intervening text...

This theory can explain the case we saw earlier (repeated):

[(1)](#foo) Sample sentence.

workaround.explanation: To actually associate an expansion with HTML, use an abbr element for a native browser tooltip, or tp-ref with a hidden tp-glossary entry for a rich hover preview. Each occurrence must be marked explicitly. These alternatives add abbreviation behavior that Pandoc itself does not provide.

examples.explanation: The blockquote renders, but its [!TIP] marker is not interpreted as an alert.
examples.originalSource:
> [!TIP]
> Helpful advice for doing things better or more easily.
examples.source:
> [!TIP]
> Helpful advice for doing things better or more easily.

workaround.explanation: Keep the blockquote and replace the alert marker with a tp-callout inside it. Prefix every line with > so the callout stays inside the quotation. Its styling follows TP rather than GitHub/Pandoc.

examples.explanation: MultiMarkdown image-reference attributes are not recognized.
examples.originalSource:
This is a reference ![image][ref] with MultiMarkdown attributes.

[ref]: https://path.to/image "Image title" width=20px height=30px
       id=myId class="myClass1 myClass2"
examples.source:
This is a reference ![image][ref] with MultiMarkdown attributes.

[ref]: https://path.to/image "Image title" width=20px height=30px
       id=myId class="myClass1 myClass2"

workaround.explanation: Replace the reference image with an inline image URL and put its attributes in braces immediately afterwards. This avoids unsupported MultiMarkdown reference attributes. The rewrite uses the bundled fixture instead of the placeholder URL.
workaround.source: This is an ![image](docs/pandoc-markdown-examples/images/sample.svg "Image title"){#myId .myClass1 .myClass2 width=20 height=30}.

examples.explanation: Unclosed superscript syntax is not recognized.

workaround.explanation: Close the superscript with a second ^, as required by TP’s paired-marker syntax.

examples.explanation: Unclosed subscript syntax is not recognized.

workaround.explanation: Close the subscript with a second ~.
workaround.source: Oxygen is O~2~.

examples.explanation: Pandoc wiki-link syntax is not resolved.

workaround.explanation: Use an ordinary Markdown link with an explicit destination. There is no wiki-page resolver; replace the sample URL with the real destination.
workaround.source: [title](https://example.org/)

examples.explanation: The alternative wiki-link ordering is not resolved.

workaround.explanation: Use an ordinary Markdown link with an explicit destination. There is no wiki-page resolver; replace the sample URL with the real destination.
workaround.source: [title](https://example.org/)
